acceptance_criteria.name: stationary_selectivity_with_B1_B2_and_release_held_PRIMARY
acceptance_criteria.rule: PRIMARY criterion for this experiment -- the graded inverted-archive candidate's stationary profile is this cycle's selected limitation (criterion 6 FAILed on BOTH of its cohorts on abstention volume, 48/240 and 64/240 against the <= 32 budget, development successes failing with it, harm passing on both). This criterion is the conjunction of four carried forms, graded per cohort, and PASSes only if ALL FOUR sides hold on the same cohort: (a) STATIONARY SIDE, criterion 6's frozen form in full (abstentions <= 32/240, successes >= recent8 - 6, harm <= recent8 on the stationary control arm); AND (b) B1 SIDE, criterion 9's frozen form in full (abstention TAKEN in at least 3 of the 6 pooled B1 onset states, at least 1 of the taken states a NON-FULL firing -- a retained partial, the only non-full class remaining after the widened class's removal -- B1 harm <= guard AND < recent8); AND (c) B2 SIDE, criterion 1's frozen form in full, with the inverted minority model carried as the candidate's minority model (minority TAKEN >= 3/6 pooled B2 onset, selectivity <= 1/6 at B1 and <= 1/6 at return-A, B2 harm <= guard AND <= 0.60 x recent8, successes >= guard + 16); AND (d) RELEASE SIDE, criterion 5's frozen form in full (including abstentions <= 36/144, successes >= recent8 - 8, non-recent8 branch in at most 1 of the 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 states, and the abstained branch in 0 of those 9 states). Criteria 6, 9, 1, 5, and 11 are ALSO graded individually below in their carried forms, so a failure of this conjunction is attributable to its exact side and sub-condition, never hidden inside the PRIMARY verdict. Every graded population is ALSO reported for the decisive baseline method (inverted_archive_minority_recovery) on the same cohort, and every state at which the two methods' taken branches differ is named with its kind, its widened_armed record, and both methods' successes / harm -- those states are, by construction, exactly the widened-armed states, so the report states exactly what the removal changed on these cohorts: how many widened firings the decisive baseline took at B1, on the control arm, and at checkpoint 32, and what each was worth. The grading cap in the grading record (a Demonstrated verdict requires at least one widened-armed graded state at which the decisive baseline abstained through the widened class and the candidate did not, in at least one cohort) applies on top of this criterion, so a conjunction PASS with zero exercised removals on both cohorts is reported as a carried-profile pass with a removal null result, never as a removal demonstration.

acceptance_criteria.name: second_switch_B2_protection_preserved
acceptance_criteria.rule: Co-graded guard, criterion 1's form carried from the preceding protocols and promoted into PRIMARY criterion 13's B2 side - graded individually so the conjunction's attribution is exact. The SINGLE changed element's exposure is exactly this criterion: branch selection (arming, joint test, purity gate, recovery precedence) is identical to the decisive baseline by construction, so sub-conditions (a) and (b) are the decisive baseline method's figures on the same cohort, while the harm and successes in (c) and (d) at minority-fired states are scored through the INVERTED minority model (see minority_model), carried unchanged. The removal's own exposure on this criterion is the fall-through at B2 states where neither recovery branch fired and the widened class would have abstained: there the candidate acts on recent8 where the decisive baseline abstained, charged here exactly as abstention firing was charged in the preceding protocols. Co-graded guard, carried over unchanged in form from the minority, reference-purity, abstention-release, and abstention-higher-corroboration protocols: the carried abstention classes (full and retained partial -- the widened class is REMOVED in this experiment) and the carried inverted minority model must together hold the B2 protection the minority branch demonstrated (abstention is not the B2 protective branch - minority recovery is, and it sits above abstention in the decision order - but abstention firing, or its removal, at B2 states where neither recovery branch fired changes those states' harm, in either direction, and that is charged here, exactly as in the widened-window protocol). Graded per cohort over the B2 pooled onset cells (checkpoints 2 and 4 x 3 seeds; 96 episode-checkpoints; engagement graded from the candidate's recorded decision records ONLY, no TEST outcomes): (a) ENGAGEMENT - the minority recovery branch is TAKEN (minority_joint_count >= 1, minority branch armed, purity gate armed, acting source minority_archive) in at least 3 of the 6 pooled B2 onset seed-checkpoint states; AND (b) SELECTIVITY - the minority recovery branch is taken in at most 1 of the 6 pooled B1 onset states AND at most 1 of the 6 pooled return-A onset states on the same cohort; AND (c) HARM - candidate harmful TEST actions pooled over the B2 onset cells <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions pooled over the same cells on the same cohort, AND candidate B2 pooled onset harm <= 0.60 * recent8 B2 pooled onset harm on the same cohort; AND (d) PRODUCTIVITY - candidate successes pooled over the B2 onset cells >= evidence_opposition_guard successes pooled over the same cells + 16. Taken states are reported split by checkpoint (2 alone vs 4 alone vs pooled), with the realized minority_fraction, minority_armed flag, reference_purity, and purity_armed flag at each, and against the records-only minority-rule and reference-purity-rule derivations (see metrics_reported). Abstention-branch firing (split by trigger kind, now including widened) and abstention-gate disarmings (by cause: leg P vs leg R vs both) at B2 are reported (with realized opposed_count, preceding_pair_opposed_count, newest4_opposed_count, and acting_opposed_count at each) but do NOT count toward sub-condition (a), as in the preceding protocols.

The widened-window protocol's own criterion-11 text, which this criterion carried verbatim through the inverted-archive protocol, is superseded here in exactly the non-full credit and the widened-reporting clauses, because the widened class no longer exists in the candidate; its population is reported records-only (widened-armed states, the decisive baseline method's widened-taken states, and the candidate's branches at those states, split by checkpoint), so the removal's exercised states remain as visible in the report as the widened class's firings were in its own cycle. acceptance_criteria.name: stationary_control_selectivity_not_given_back
acceptance_criteria.rule: Co-graded guard, carried in the identical frozen form from the widened-window protocol (the stationary side of criterion 11) through the inverted-archive protocol, where it FAILed on both cohorts; here it is PRIMARY criterion 13's stationary side and this experiment's selected limitation in its exact frozen form, graded individually. Co-graded guard, carried in the identical frozen form from the preceding protocols - the stationary side of PRIMARY criterion 11, graded individually so the conjunction's attribution is exact. In the preceding generation this criterion PASSed on development at exact recent8 parity (0/240 abstentions, 110 = 110 successes, 130 = 130 harm - a leg-retention pass: the partial-purity-rule took 2 control states and leg R disarmed both) and FAILed on additional by 1 success on ONE carried FULL firing (seed 443017 k=2, purity 0.889), leg R having disarmed all three partial stationary states there. What remains priced is exactly what preceded the widened class: full firings untouched by any leg, and retained partials at the preceding-pair rate (union stationary trigger expectation 0.108 raw / 0.072 adjusted per state, ~1.6 / ~1.1 firings per cohort). Graded per cohort, on the stationary control arm pooled across checkpoints 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32 (240 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 32 of 240, AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 6, AND (c) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions. The realized reference_purity, opposed_count, preceding_pair_opposed_count, newest4_opposed_count, acting_opposed_count, and abstention_trigger_kind on the control arm are recorded and reported at every checkpoint, alongside the realized minority_fraction and minority_armed values exactly as in the preceding protocols; every control checkpoint at which the candidate's taken branch differs from the records-only preceding-pair-rule derivation (in particular every WIDENED state, which the graded preceding-pair candidate would not have taken) and from the records-only partial-purity-rule and purity-only-rule derivations, and every abstention that was taken, is stated explicitly in the report, with the taken or disarmed state's purity, opposed counts, and trigger kind named. If no stationary widened trigger survived on a cohort, the PASS is reported with the widened-armed and widened-disarmed counts stated - not as a no-trigger PASS, since the widened-rule derivation states how many widened triggers existed.

acceptance_criteria.name: release_and_productivity_by_checkpoint_32
acceptance_criteria.rule: Co-graded guard, carried in the identical frozen form from the widened-window protocol, graded individually; it is also PRIMARY criterion 13's release side. The inverted minority model's exposure here is direct and carried: any checkpoint-32 minority routing is scored through the inverted model (the inverted cycle's additional-cohort failure and Regression were exactly two such routings), and sub-conditions (b) and (c) charge it exactly as the carried form charged minority routings. The removal's exposure here inverts the widened protocols': a checkpoint-32 state the decisive baseline abstains from through the widened class is ACTED on by the candidate, and its outcome is charged under (b) and (c) in the opposite direction. Co-graded guard - the graded partial candidate PASSed it on the additional cohort and FAILed it on development on the records sub-condition (c) alone (2 of 9 non-recent8 states, both carried minority routings, abstained branch 0 of 9 on both cohorts, the development zero via an exercised leg-P release at purity 0.658 and the additional zero via two leg-P-disarmed return-A partial triggers); all four sub-conditions are carried unchanged in form, and neither the preceding-pair leg nor the widened class's removal may give any of them back - sub-condition (d) is the exposed one on the abstention side: for partial triggers, at checkpoint 32 the preceding pair shares the newest pair's segment, so a late partial trigger's leg-R retention is segment-dependent; the widened class no longer exists, so no late widened abstention can occur -- but a state the decisive baseline abstains from at checkpoint 32 through the widened class is acted on here, and sub-conditions (b) and (c) charge its outcomed, since neither had a widened class. Graded per cohort, pooled across stages B1, return_A, and B2 at checkpoint 32 (144 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 36 of 144 (25 percent), AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 8 (carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols), AND (c) from the candidate's decision records alone, among the 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 seed-checkpoint states (3 stages x 3 seeds), the candidate takes a non-recent8 branch (retained_archive, minority_archive, or abstained) in at most 1 state - the carried records-level release measure for the recovery branches - AND (d) the candidate takes the ABSTAINED branch in 0 of those 9 states (carried from the preceding protocols: both combined-gate generations and the partial generation removed abstention from the late records on both cohorts; the preceding-pair leg must hold that at zero for partial triggers, not merely at the carried allowance). The realized reference_purity, purity_armed, opposing counts (newest opposed_count, preceding_pair_opposed_count, newest4_opposed_count, acting_opposed_count, and supporting_opposed_count) and abstention_trigger_kind at all 9 states are reported alongside, split by branch taken, so the report distinguishes a leg-P release of a late abstention (trigger present, purity disarmed, fell through to recent8), a leg-R release of a late PARTIAL abstention (trigger partial, purity armed, preceding_pair_opposed_count == 0, fell through to recent8), a late WIDENED trigger released by leg P (kind widened, purity disarmed) or never armed (widened_armed false), and a state where no abstention trigger of any class was present at all, and likewise distinguishes the recovery branches' purity releases as in the preceding protocols.

budgets.abstention_budget: Criteria 13(a) / 11 / 6 bound abstention's downstream cost on the stationary control arm (at most 32 of 240) and criterion 5 bounds it at checkpoint 32 (at most 36 of 144, plus 0 abstained states among the 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 states under criterion 5(d)); criteria 13(b) / 11 / 9 set a FLOOR, not a budget, on B1 onset protective abstention (>= 3 of 6 states taken, at least 1 of them a retained-partial firing). With the widened class removed, the abstention population is the full and retained-partial classes only: the published-rate stationary expectation is ~26 raw / ~17 adjusted episodes per cohort, inside the 32 budget in expectation under both rate pairs -- the first cycle in this line whose frozen design is inside its own stationary budget in expectation on raw rates as well as adjusted (the widened union sat at ~39 raw). Abstention disarmed under stable disagreement is the carried-over release mechanism, not a budget violation; abstention blocked by leg P or leg R is recorded separately by cause and is likewise not a budget violation -- its onset cost is graded through criteria 13, 11, 9, 1, 3, and 4. There is no widened abstention to budget: a candidate abstention recorded with kind widened, or at a widened-armed-only state, is an implementation defect under criterion 7.
budgets.harm_budget: Criterion 13(b) / 9: candidate B1 pooled onset harm at most the evidence_opposition_guard baseline's B1 pooled onset harm on the SAME cohort and strictly below recent8's, as carried. Criterion 13(c) / 1(c): candidate B2 pooled onset harm at most the guard's and at most 60 percent of recent8's on the same cohort, as carried from the inverted-archive protocol (where it PASSed on both cohorts: 19 vs guard 28 / ceiling 39.6 development, 46 vs guard 74 / ceiling 54.0 additional -- now a PRIMARY side, so a repeat failure here fails the PRIMARY). Criterion 3: candidate pooled onset (all stages, checkpoints 2 and 4) harm at most the guard's, with at least 5 of 6 individual onset cells at or below recent8. Criterion 4: candidate pooled return-A onset harm at most the guard's and at most 60 percent of recent8's. The removal's fall-through harm is NOT hidden by these budgets: at every state where the decisive baseline abstained through the widened class and the candidate acted, the candidate's realized harm at that state is reported against the abstention's zero, per state, in the grading report.
budgets.train_actor_harm: No cap is claimed: the external actor's harm is a fixed cost of the shared evidence stream, identical for all methods, and is published in full per seed (criterion 7). It is never hidden inside or netted against TEST results.

expected_failure_modes: Removal null / equivalence (pre-registered): the widened class fired zero stationary firings on its own cohorts and its pooled-onset published rate is ~0.014 raw / ~0.020 adjusted per state, so on these draws the decisive baseline method may take no widened firing in any graded population -- candidate and decisive baseline then agree everywhere, criterion 6's outcome is whatever the carried classes produce, and the removal demonstrated nothing. The grading cap (a Demonstrated verdict requires at least one widened-armed graded state at which the decisive baseline abstained through the widened class and the candidate did not, in at least one cohort) applies; widened-armed and widened-taken counts are reported for both methods at every graded population, not buried.

Non-full B1 absence (pre-registered, the cycle's central engagement-side risk): with the widened class removed, criterion 9's non-full sub-condition rests on the retained-partial class alone -- expected ~1.0 raw / ~1.5 adjusted partial B1 firings per cohort at trigger level, probability of at least one ~0.68 raw / ~0.82 adjusted before leg P, leg R, and the carried authority are applied. A cohort whose taken B1 states are all full-class fails criterion 9 (and PRIMARY criterion 13) on the non-full sub-condition even at 3/6 or better engagement -- charged, not excused, and reported with the partial states' disarming causes (leg R at preceding 0, leg P, authority) stated per state.

Carried-class stationary survival (pre-registered, the cycle's central cost-side risk): removal cuts the union's stationary trigger expectation by about a third, it does not zero it -- ~1.6 raw / ~1.1 adjusted control firings per cohort are still expected from the full and retained-partial classes, and criterion 6(b)'s margin is -6 successes for the whole arm. One carried firing at a control state where recent8 scores 7 or more consumes the entire margin unless a productive control recovery offsets it (the widened cycle's development arm offset exactly this way; the preceding-pair cycle's additional arm failed by 1 on one carried FULL firing). Charged against criteria 13 / 11 / 6, not excused; every surviving control state's kind, purity, and counts are stated in the report.

B1 engagement draw failure (bounded, recorded): the removal costs ~0.1 of a B1 state per cohort in trigger expectation, but draws vary: a cohort realizing few full triggers (the full class's adjusted onset rate is 0.449 per state) and no retained partial can fall below criterion 9's 3-of-6 floor for both the candidate and the records-only derivations alike. The failure is charged to this experiment's criteria, not excused as a draw property; the decisive baseline method's taken count on the same cohort is reported alongside so the removal's own share of any shortfall (at most the widened-taken states) is exact.

Checkpoint-32 exposure without the widened class (pre-registered): the inverted cycle's additional-cohort Regression was two non-recent8 minority routings at k=32, a mechanism the removal does not touch -- criterion 5(c) and the checkpoint-32 Regression clause remain fully exposed through the carried recovery branches, and the inverted model still scores any B2 k=32 minority routing. On the abstention side the exposure inverts: a late state the decisive baseline would have abstained from through the widened class is now ACTED on (recent8, or a recovery branch) by the candidate -- if that state's recent8 outcome is harmful, the cost appears in criterion 5(b)/(c) comparisons and in the k=32 successes line exactly as a taken abstention's cost would have, in the opposite direction. All 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 states are reported with branch, kind, widened_armed, and scores, as in the preceding protocols.

B2 / return-A fall-through changes (bounded, recorded): abstention sits below both recovery branches, so the removal changes a B2 or return-A state only where neither recovery branch fired and the widened class would have abstained -- there the candidate acts on recent8 where the decisive baseline abstained, changing that state's successes and harm in either direction. Charged through criteria 1, 4, 3, and 13 exactly as abstention firing was charged in the preceding protocols; per-state branch attribution is reported in full so a fall-through change is never attributed to the minority model, nor a minority-model outcome to the removal.

Stationary benefit is expectation-level (stated in advance): the published-rate arithmetic shows the union WITH the widened class outside criterion 6(a) in raw expectation (~39 episodes) and the union WITHOUT it inside on both pairs (~26 raw / ~17 adjusted) -- but per-cohort realized firings are small integers with wide dispersion (the widened cycle realized zero widened stationary firings against a ~0.8 raw expectation). A criterion 6 PASS on these cohorts therefore does not by itself prove the removal caused it, and a FAIL does not by itself prove the carried classes cannot hold the margins on any draw; the report must state the candidate-vs-decisive-baseline control-arm difference exactly (states, episodes, successes) so the removal's realized effect on these cohorts is separated from the carried classes' draw.

Inversion-structure limit (carried over, stated): the carried minority branch and its inverted model exploit this simulator's exact-inversion structure (B is the precise progress / damage inversion of A). Any PASS remains bounded to this inversion simulator -- evidence about abstention class composition for a two-switch onset family, in this simulator only, not a general abstention-selectivity solution, not calibrated uncertainty, and not real-world safety.

fixed_parameters.decision_rule_rationale: The abstention line's successive questions are answered (gate composition does not bind B1; the newest-pair trigger binds it in both directions; four-event corroboration holds the partial stationary arm but engages nothing on its own cohorts; the widened acting-window class restored B1 engagement on its cohorts and held stationary selectivity there, then, carried unchanged, was part of a profile whose stationary volume failed on both of the inverted-archive cycle's cohorts), and the inverted-archive grading isolated the failure to the carried abstention classes' stationary selectivity while demonstrating the minority model change (criterion 1 PASS on both cohorts). This cycle therefore varies the one abstention element the published rates indict -- the widened class's composition membership -- and nothing else: the full and retained-partial classes, leg P, leg R, the authority condition, both recovery branches including the inverted minority model, and the acting model are the graded inverted-archive candidate's, bit for bit, so branch selection is identical except at widened-armed states and every outcome difference against the decisive baseline method is attributable to the removal. A gating alternative (a new leg on any recorded quantity) was considered at the selection stage and rejected on the recorded evidence, not on taste: no recorded quantity descriptively separates the stationary-fired and B1-taken populations on the inspected draws, so a gate threshold would be fitted to inspected per-state counts. A threshold raise for the widened class was considered and rejected on the published-rate scan: >= 4 is removal at onset with a residual stationary tail, strictly dominated. The removal has no threshold to tune: it is the unique class-composition change the published rate pairs define, since the widened class is the only selectivity-negative class under both.

fixed_parameters.minority_archive: IDENTICAL to the graded minority-archive, reference-purity, abstention-release, and abstention-higher-corroboration candidates, unchanged and not re-tuned. Computed from the retained archive (events[:N-26]) and its own per-span majorities only. For each archive event e: let M(e) be the archive expectation for span(e) under the unchanged archive concordance definition (strictly-highest reported class among archive events of that span; tie or empty gives null). e is ARCHIVE-MATCHED if M(e) is progress or damage AND e's reported class is progress or damage. e is MINORITY (discordant) if archive-matched AND e's reported class DIFFERS from M(e). The MINORITY SET is the set of all minority archive events, in chronological order. minority_matched_count (over the archive) = number of archive-matched archive events; minority_discordant_count = size of the minority set; minority_fraction = minority_discordant_count / minority_matched_count (0 if minority_matched_count == 0). fixed_parameters.minority_concordance_test: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, the MINORITY EXPECTATION for span(e) is the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among MINORITY-SET events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null). e is MINORITY-MATCHED if its minority expectation is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is MINORITY-CONCORDANT if minority-matched and its reported class EQUALS the minority expectation. minority_concordant_count and minority_matched_count (over the newest window) are in 0..2 and are recorded in full, with per-event minority records exactly as in the graded candidates.
fixed_parameters.minority_joint_test: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, e is MINORITY-JOINT if it is MINORITY-CONCORDANT AND reference-OPPOSED (extended 50-event reference, unchanged) - both flags on the SAME event. minority_joint_count in 0..2, recorded in full with per-event minority joint flags.
fixed_parameters.minority_model: CARRIED UNCHANGED from the graded inverted-archive candidate (in that experiment this was the single changed element; here it is carried, and the single changed element is the widened class's removal -- see widened_class_removal). The estimator, action scoring (utility 3 * p(progress) - 10 * p(damage), deterministic action-id tie break, via RelationOutcomeMemory.choose), and checkpoint / replay mechanics are the existing ones, unchanged. In the graded candidates the minority model was fitted on the MINORITY SET events only; here the minority set is still computed in full and still drives minority arming (fraction / discordant count), the minority concordance and joint records, and every recorded minority field - it is no longer the model's training set. fixed_parameters.preceding_pair_leg: CARRIED UNCHANGED from the graded inverted-archive candidate (in the preceding-pair experiment this leg was the single new element; here it is carried bit-for-bit, and the single changed element is the widened class's removal -- see widened_class_removal). Computed from the observed reported stream only. The PRECEDING PAIR is the two events immediately before the newest pair in the observed stream: events[N-4] and events[N-3] (0-based), i.e. events[-4:-2]. Each preceding-pair event is scored EXACTLY as an acting-window record is scored in the graded candidates: against the SAME extended 50-event reference window's per-span majorities (strictly-highest reported class wins, tie or empty gives null; matched iff expectation and reported class are both progress or damage; opposed iff matched and different). preceding_pair_matched_count and preceding_pair_opposed_count are in 0..2 and are recorded in full with the per-event preceding-pair records. LEG R is ARMED iff preceding_pair_opposed_count >= 1 (PRECEDING_PAIR_THRESHOLD = 1). fixed_parameters.recovery_model: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on the retained archive events only (events[:N-26]), with the existing estimator and action scoring (utility 3 * p(progress) - 10 * p(damage), deterministic action-id tie break, via RelationOutcomeMemory.choose).
fixed_parameters.reference_purity_gate: CARRIED OVER IDENTICALLY from the graded reference-purity candidate, unchanged and not re-tuned, and applied to the two RECOVERY branches exactly as graded there. Computed from the extended reference window (the 50 events immediately preceding the newest window, indices N-52 .. N-3 - the SAME window the immediate signal reads) and its own per-span majorities only. For each reference event e: let R(e) be the reference expectation for span(e), i.e. the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among REFERENCE events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null). e is REFERENCE-MATCHED if R(e) is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is REFERENCE-CONCORDANT if reference-matched AND e's reported class EQUALS R(e). reference_matched_count and reference_concordant_count are over the 50 reference events; reference_purity = reference_concordant_count / reference_matched_count (0 if reference_matched_count == 0). The purity gate is ARMED iff reference_purity >= 0.70. Regular recovery fires iff joint_count >= 1 AND the carried-over recovery authority is armed AND the purity gate is armed; minority recovery fires iff minority_joint_count >= 1 AND the minority branch is armed AND the purity gate is armed (and regular recovery did not fire, per the decision order). A recovery trigger blocked by purity alone is recorded (recovery_disarmed_by_purity / minority_disarmed_by_purity) and falls through. In this experiment the same purity quantity and threshold ADDITIONALLY form the sole leg of the abstention gate (see abstention_gate), exactly the role leg P played inside both graded release gates - with leg S removed, not with any quantity re-derived or re-tuned.
fixed_parameters.retained_archive: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: every observed event BEFORE the original reference partition, indices 0 .. N-27, i.e. events[:N-26]. Not phase-segmented, not a snapshot, and receives no phase, stage, or switch information.
fixed_parameters.threshold_justification: Fixed a priori from the simulator's known noise rates, the preceding experiments' published graded aggregates and decision records, and this simulator's published segment geometry, not from any score of this experiment (none exist). (i) THE CHANGED ELEMENT HAS NO THRESHOLD: removing a trigger class is a composition change, not a tuned parameter. Its design values are consequences of the published rates and geometry, stated in the hypothesis and derived in full in the arithmetic kept with the campaign state: per-class pooled-onset / stationary trigger rates under both published rate pairs (full 0.701 / 0.026 raw, 0.449 / 0.017 adjusted; retained partial 0.173 / 0.081, 0.251 / 0.055; widened-only 0.014 / 0.056, 0.020 / 0.034), the widened class the only one with stationary rate above its pooled-onset rate under both pairs; the >= 4 alternative scanned and strictly dominated (0.002 / 0.006 raw, 0.002 / 0.003 adjusted). No alternative composition (removing the partial class instead; removing the full class; keeping widened but gating it on a recorded quantity) is frozen, because the rate scan indicts only the widened class (the other two classes are selectivity-positive pooled under both pairs), and a gate on a recorded quantity has no honest derivation after the selection stage's separability finding. (ii) PRIMARY FLOORS AND MARGINS CARRIED, NOT RE-TUNED: criterion 13 conjoins criterion 6's stationary form (abstentions <= 32/240, successes >= recent8 - 6, harm <= recent8), criterion 9's B1 form (engagement >= 3 of 6 with >= 1 non-full firing -- now a retained partial, the only non-full class remaining, its form carried from the preceding-pair protocol where partial was likewise the credited non-full class -- B1 harm <= guard AND < recent8), criterion 1's B2 form (engagement >= 3 of 6, selectivity <= 1 of 6 at B1 and at return-A, harm <= guard AND <= 0.60 x recent8, successes >= guard + 16, with the inverted minority model carried as the candidate's minority model), and criterion 5's release form (incl. abstained branch 0/9), every component carried at its frozen value from the inverted-archive protocol, which carried them from its predecessors. (iii) ALL thresholds carried unchanged: leg P at reference_purity >= 0.70, full trigger at opposed_count == 2, partial trigger at opposed_count == 1, leg R at preceding_pair_opposed_count >= 1, minority arming at fraction >= 0.25 AND discordant >= 8, joint tests at count >= 1, authority strict-majority D * 2 > C in both windows, corroboration at recent_concordant_count >= 2 -- none re-tuned against any inspected cohort, and in particular the widened threshold is NOT raised to a value fitted to the inverted cohorts' realized acting counts: the class is removed on its published rates, or not at all.
fixed_parameters.widened_window_trigger: REMOVED in this experiment -- see widened_class_removal. The graded definition is retained here for the record only: newest4_opposed_count <= 1 AND acting_opposed_count >= 3 over the last 8 events, behind leg P + carried authority, disjoint from the full and retained-partial classes by construction. In this candidate that condition is computed and recorded (widened_armed, records-only) and never fires.
fixed_parameters.widened_class_removal: THE SINGLE CHANGED ELEMENT. The widened abstention trigger class of the graded widened-window and inverted-archive candidates -- newest4_opposed_count <= 1 AND acting_opposed_count >= 3 over the last 8 events, behind leg P -- is REMOVED: it is not a trigger, not a gate leg, and not a branch input anywhere in this candidate. The abstention branch has exactly TWO trigger classes, identical to the graded preceding-pair candidate's: FULL (opposed_count == 2, behind leg P) and PARTIAL (opposed_count == 1, behind leg P + leg R). abstention_trigger_kind takes values full / partial / none only -- never widened. The widened quantities are still COMPUTED AND RECORDED, records-only, exactly as the graded candidates record them (newest4_opposed_count, widened_armed -- whether the removed class WOULD have armed -- and widened_threshold recorded as 3), so the removed class's would-be population is recomputable from this candidate's records at every checkpoint and the records-only widened-rule derivation (the decisive baseline's abstention rule) remains checkable against the decisive baseline method's taken states. No other element changes: acting model (recent8 exactly), extended signal, retained archive, archive concordance, joint test (joint_count >= 1), recovery model, the full three-leg authority condition, the minority branch in full INCLUDING the inverted minority model carried unchanged from the graded inverted-archive candidate, leg P >= 0.70 on both recovery branches and as the abstention gate's leg, leg R on partial triggers only, and support threshold null -- verified at implementation by a diff against the graded inverted-archive candidate: the ONLY code differences are the widened class's removal from the trigger / kind / gate composition, its docstring, and names/schema.

Non-full B1 absence (pre-registered, the cycle's central engagement-side risk): with the widened class removed, criterion 9's non-full sub-condition rests on the retained-partial class alone -- expected ~1.0 raw / ~1.5 adjusted partial B1 firings per cohort at trigger level, probability of at least one ~0.68 raw / ~0.82 adjusted before leg P, leg R, and the carried authority are applied. A cohort whose taken B1 states are all full-class fails criterion 9 (and PRIMARY criterion 13) on the non-full sub-condition even at 3/6 or better engagement -- charged, not excused, and reported with the partial states' disarming causes (leg R at preceding 0, leg P, authority) stated per state.

Carried-class stationary survival (pre-registered, the cycle's central cost-side risk): removal cuts the union's stationary trigger expectation by about a third, it does not zero it -- ~1.6 raw / ~1.1 adjusted control firings per cohort are still expected from the full and retained-partial classes, and criterion 6(b)'s margin is -6 successes for the whole arm. One carried firing at a control state where recent8 scores 7 or more consumes the entire margin unless a productive control recovery offsets it (the widened cycle's development arm offset exactly this way; the preceding-pair cycle's additional arm failed by 1 on one carried FULL firing). Charged against criteria 13 / 11 / 6, not excused; every surviving control state's kind, purity, and counts are stated in the report.

B1 engagement draw failure (bounded, recorded): the removal costs ~0.1 of a B1 state per cohort in trigger expectation, but draws vary: a cohort realizing few full triggers (the full class's adjusted onset rate is 0.449 per state) and no retained partial can fall below criterion 9's 3-of-6 floor for both the candidate and the records-only derivations alike. The failure is charged to this experiment's criteria, not excused as a draw property; the decisive baseline method's taken count on the same cohort is reported alongside so the removal's own share of any shortfall (at most the widened-taken states) is exact.

Checkpoint-32 exposure without the widened class (pre-registered): the inverted cycle's additional-cohort Regression was two non-recent8 minority routings at k=32, a mechanism the removal does not touch -- criterion 5(c) and the checkpoint-32 Regression clause remain fully exposed through the carried recovery branches, and the inverted model still scores any B2 k=32 minority routing. On the abstention side the exposure inverts: a late state the decisive baseline would have abstained from through the widened class is now ACTED on (recent8, or a recovery branch) by the candidate -- if that state's recent8 outcome is harmful, the cost appears in criterion 5(b)/(c) comparisons and in the k=32 successes line exactly as a taken abstention's cost would have, in the opposite direction. All 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 states are reported with branch, kind, widened_armed, and scores, as in the preceding protocols.

B2 / return-A fall-through changes (bounded, recorded): abstention sits below both recovery branches, so the removal changes a B2 or return-A state only where neither recovery branch fired and the widened class would have abstained -- there the candidate acts on recent8 where the decisive baseline abstained, changing that state's successes and harm in either direction. Charged through criteria 1, 4, 3, and 13 exactly as abstention firing was charged in the preceding protocols; per-state branch attribution is reported in full so a fall-through change is never attributed to the minority model, nor a minority-model outcome to the removal.

Stationary benefit is expectation-level (stated in advance): the published-rate arithmetic shows the union WITH the widened class outside criterion 6(a) in raw expectation (~39 episodes) and the union WITHOUT it inside on both pairs (~26 raw / ~17 adjusted) -- but per-cohort realized firings are small integers with wide dispersion (the widened cycle realized zero widened stationary firings against a ~0.8 raw expectation). A criterion 6 PASS on these cohorts therefore does not by itself prove the removal caused it, and a FAIL does not by itself prove the carried classes cannot hold the margins on any draw; the report must state the candidate-vs-decisive-baseline control-arm difference exactly (states, episodes, successes) so the removal's realized effect on these cohorts is separated from the carried classes' draw.

Inversion-structure limit (carried over, stated): the carried minority branch and its inverted model exploit this simulator's exact-inversion structure (B is the precise progress / damage inversion of A). Any PASS remains bounded to this inversion simulator -- evidence about abstention class composition for a two-switch onset family, in this simulator only, not a general abstention-selectivity solution, not calibrated uncertainty, and not real-world safety.

hypothesis: The selection stage's records-only evidence review established two things. First, criterion 6's failure in the inverted-archive cycle is a selectivity / productivity failure, not a harm failure: abstention volume failed on both cohorts (48/240 and 64/240 against the <= 32 budget) and development successes failed with it, while harm passed on both. Second, stated honestly, NO recorded quantity descriptively separates the stationary-fired population from the B1-taken population on the inspected draws -- every recorded field's interval overlaps across the two populations (purity, acting_opposed_count, newest4_opposed_count, opposed_count, preceding-pair count, supporting count, checkpoint), and one full configuration occurs verbatim in both. A new GATE on any recorded quantity therefore has no honest derivation: any threshold frozen on those fields would be tuning against inspected per-state counts, which this campaign's discipline forbids. The remaining honest lever is the classes' composition, judged on the simulator's published rates alone, and on those rates the three classes are NOT symmetric (full derivation from the published rate pairs -- raw p = 0.1625 / q = 0.8375 and matched-adjusted p ~ 0.13 / q ~ 0.67 -- and the segment geometry only, kept with the campaign state; no inspected count was used): the full class's pooled-onset trigger rate is 0.701 raw / 0.449 adjusted per state against a stationary rate of 0.026 / 0.017 (selectivity ratio ~26x under both pairs); the retained-partial class's is 0.173 / 0.251 pooled onset against 0.081 / 0.055 stationary (positive pooled, its checkpoint-2 arm exactly stationary-rate on raw rates -- the priced, already-graded cost of leg R); the widened class at its frozen threshold >= 3 is the ONLY class that is selectivity-NEGATIVE under BOTH rate pairs -- pooled onset 0.014 raw / 0.020 adjusted per state against stationary 0.056 / 0.034 -- because its newest4 <= 1 condition excludes exactly the onset states where post-switch evidence has accumulated in the newest four, while on the stationary arm newest4 <= 1 is the common case (~0.87 raw / ~0.92 adjusted of states) and acting >= 3 is a pure noise tail. The widened class carries 34.1 percent raw / 31.8 percent adjusted of the union's stationary trigger rate but only 1.5 / 2.7 percent of its pooled-onset trigger rate. Raising its threshold to >= 4 is strictly dominated (pooled onset collapses to 0.002 / 0.002 -- a class that cannot fire at onset -- while a stationary tail of 0.006 / 0.003 survives), so removal is the unique non-dominated disposition the published rates define, with no free threshold to tune. Expected effect, trigger level before leg P and the carried authority (which apply identically to candidate and decisive baseline): the union's stationary rate falls from 0.163 raw / 0.105 adjusted to 0.108 / 0.072 per state -- about 1.6 raw / 1.1 adjusted expected control firings per cohort, ~26 / ~17 of 240 episodes, inside criterion 6(a)'s budget in expectation under both rate pairs, where the union WITH the widened class sits at ~39 raw episodes, outside it -- at a pooled-onset trigger cost of ~0.014 raw / ~0.020 adjusted per state (~0.1 of a B1 state per cohort), which the full class's onset rate absorbs against criterion 9's 3-of-6 floor in expectation (union pooled onset 0.875 raw / 0.700 adjusted per state, ~5.25 / ~4.20 of 6 states trigger-level). The hypothesis is genuinely open in both directions, and this protocol states the other side in advance: criterion 9's non-full credit now rests on the retained-partial class alone (expected ~1.0 raw / ~1.5 adjusted partial B1 firings per cohort trigger-level, probability of at least one ~0.68 raw / ~0.82 adjusted before leg P, leg R, and authority), so a cohort can pass the 3-of-6 floor on full firings and still fail the non-full sub-condition; removal does nothing to the carried classes' own stationary firings, so criterion 6(b)'s -6 success margin remains exposed to where ~1-2 expected control firings land (one firing at a state where recent8 scores >= 7 consumes the whole margin unless offset by productive control recovery, exactly as in the preceding generations); and on the widened class's own cohorts its stationary arm never fired at all, so the removal's benefit is an expectation over draws, not a mechanism that must appear on these cohorts -- if no widened-armed state is taken by the decisive baseline method anywhere in the graded populations, the removal is a null on these draws and the grading cap says so.
